texts: rage hurts me most
hey can u write a doha about how losing my temper never solves anything
Write a doha about how a person who gives in to rage destroys his own peace of mind, loses friends and respect, and ends up suffering far more than the one he was furious with.
Wrath devours first the one who nurtures it, and leaves him poorer than before.
I yelled at my father tonight, said things I can never take back, and I have not felt right in my own skin since.
doha on anger w a traveler and a skeleton, how rage leads nowhere
traveler, skeleton, angry temper
On the road I watched a traveler fight a stranger over a trivial matter, and it made me think of the skeleton we all become; why waste breath in rage?
Compose a doha for the traveler who loses his temper over small insults on the road, forgetting that the skeleton awaits every one of us, so fury is a heavy load that serves no one on the journey.
O traveler, why carry rage along the road when the skeleton at its end will laugh at your fury?
calm down, doha please
I need a doha about how a quick temper makes a wise man foolish in a moment, since in rage he cannot tell right from wrong, and what he does in that blind hour he regrets for years afterwards.
doha on counting to ten before reacting, my temper is awful
My husband and I fought again over the smallest thing, and afterwards both of us sat in silence feeling sick over what we said.
When wrath rises, reason departs; the wise man too becomes a child, and weeps afterwards at what he broke.
Please write a doha on how a hot temper hurts the one who holds it more than the one it is aimed at, because it ruins his sleep, his health and his judgment while the other person simply walks away.
Rage is a cup of bitterness that the angry drink themselves, hoping another will taste its sting.
Three days after the fight with my brother I am still lying awake replaying it, while he is probably sleeping fine.
doha: being angry at someone only hurts urself
anger harms the angry
Let fury settle like dust after the road, and in its stillness the mind will see clearly again.
I was so angry at my landlord that I forgot to eat all day, and he never even noticed.
forgive, let rage go
Compose a doha reminding me that holding on to fury at someone is like drinking bitterness myself and waiting for them to fall ill, and that peace begins the moment I loosen my grip on rage.
doha pls about letting go of a grudge fueled by rage
my boss made me so mad today, doha on cooling down?
The traffic cop humiliated me in front of my kids, and I wanted to shout until I lost my voice, but I only stood there shaking.
Compose a doha about the moment just before an outburst, when a wise person pauses, breathes and chooses silence over insults, because rage once spoken is a deed that cannot be taken back.
cool temper, calm mind
Between the spark of wrath and the word of rage lies a breath; blessed is he who rests in it.
doha with a water pot and ash, about how rage just leaves u empty
My mother broke the water pot in a rage, and later she sat sweeping up the ash and the pieces, not saying a word.
Write a doha showing that a person's rage can crack the pot of water that sustains him, leaving only ash where there was once a happy gathering, and that nothing is gained by such wild fury.
Rage cracks the pot of water and leaves behind only ash; what was once cool is now a ruin.
water pot, ash, furious temper
Write a doha about how a man who gives way to rage is like a madman, shouting at those he loves, breaking what he can never mend, and then weeping when the damage is done and the room is silent.
The angry mind is a blind rider upon a mad horse, and neither knows where the road ends.
doha on how rage makes ppl do stupid stuff
rage makes fools
I threw my phone against the wall during an argument and now I have a cracked screen and a broken friendship.
Whenever my temper rises I feel it tighten around my chest like a rope, and I cannot breathe until I walk away.
rope, restrain temper
Compose a doha showing that a person's wrath ties him up like a rope, binding his hands, his speech and his judgment, until he can only be freed by calm patience and forgiveness.
doha: rage is like a rope that chokes u
The rope of wrath binds the very hand that tied it, and the one who tugs it hardest falls.
Rage is a rope around one's own neck; the shroud waits for the angry and the calm alike, so why waste breath on fury?
Please write a doha explaining that the rope of wrath ties a man to endless quarrels, though the shroud awaits him just the same, so he should spend his short days in peace rather than in rage.
doha with a rope and a shroud, abt how anger is a waste
My uncle fought with his own brothers over a tiny share of land until he died, and his body was wrapped in the shroud without a single reconciliation.
rope, shroud, angry man
temper, doha, calm
hey I have a short temper at work, could u make a doha that helps
My teenage daughter says I always shout, and she is right; I want to be a gentler parent from tomorrow.
O angry heart, be still as the night is still, and let the morning find you wiser.

Please write a doha explaining that the most dangerous enemy is not outside but within, that is, the rage in our own chest, because it can destroy in one moment what patience has built over many years.
I want a doha comparing a short-tempered person to a crow that caws loudly and fights at every meal, driving all others away, while the calm one is welcomed everywhere and sits at peace with all.
The crow outside our window screams at every other bird, and I realised I act the same way when I come back from work tired and furious.
doha idea: angry ppl are like a noisy crow, nobody likes them
crow, hot temper
The crow caws in rage at the empty sky, and all the flock flies away from him.
can u do a doha about rage being like a furnace on a mountain, hot and scary
On the mountain the furnace roars, and none dares go near; so too is the man whose rage forever glows.
My father is the kind of man who goes silent and red like a furnace for hours, and the whole family waits for him to cool off, like waiting at the foot of a mountain.

Write a doha showing that the furnace on a lonely mountain consumes all that comes near it, just as a wrathful person scorches everyone around him, until he is left alone in the cold ashes of his fury.
furnace, mountain, rage
fire, rage, ruin
doha on how anger is a fire that burns u first
The fire of wrath leaps from heart to hand, and what it leaves behind is neither warm nor wise.
After I let my temper flare at the office, the fire spread to everyone, and by evening three colleagues were not speaking to me.
Write me a doha showing that rage is a fire which consumes the one who carries it before it ever touches another, so the wise man puts it out with patience before it destroys his own peace of mind.
I screamed at a junior at work today and he looked at me like I was a mountain about to fall on him; I must change.
mountain, rage
Write me a doha showing that a person's rage grows like a mountain with every harsh remark, until it blocks all the paths to friendship and he can no longer see the sky beyond it.
doha about a mountain of anger inside me, help
A mountain of fury blocks the sky of friendship; only forgiveness can wear it down over years.
doha where temper is a diamond that cuts glass but breaks the owner?
A diamond of wrath cuts any glass, yet scratches the hand that wears it, till the mountain of pride cracks.
Compose a doha showing that one angry outburst can shatter a friendship as precious as a diamond, and that the mountain of regret one builds afterwards is far heavier than the moment of satisfaction.
My wife says I threw away a diamond of a friendship at the foot of a mountain of petty arguments, all because of my temper.
diamond, mountain, hot temper
The stone I threw in my fury hit my own window, and the sun that morning showed me only the mess I had made.
stone, sun, wrath
Write a doha about how a thrown stone can never be recalled, and just so a word of rage hurled at someone remains forever, while the rising sun each day gives us a chance to start anew in calm.
The stone once thrown cannot be called back, but the sun rises gently each day to teach us patience.
doha on throwing stones in anger and what the sun teaches us
doha on rage, a forest and a house, thx
forest, house, rage
Wrath in the forest leaps from bough to bough, but wrath inside a house leaves a family of ashes.
My brother and I stopped talking after our fight in the old house, and now the path to the forest where we played as kids is overgrown.
Please write a doha showing that a man who brings his rage into his own house ruins its peace, and that no walk in the forest can heal what an angry word in the family has cracked.
A yogi in the hills once told me my red face and trembling hands showed I was lost to my temper; I still remember that.
The yogi sits unmoved while the world rages; for him wrath is a passing wind that cannot shake the still mind.
doha on how even a yogi struggles with rage
yogi, calm over rage
Write a doha showing that the yogi's true victory is not over the world but over his own temper, for a man who has conquered rage has conquered himself and is truly free in all places.
doha abt how anger gets sifted out with a winnowing fan and tested on a touchstone
winnowing fan, touchstone, rage
My teacher says my rage is the chaff of me, and a day of patience tests me like a touchstone tests metal; I want a poem on this.
Let the winnowing fan blow the husk of fury away, and the touchstone of patience show what remains.

Compose a doha showing that the winnowing fan of calm thought separates the chaff of rage from the grain of the mind, and that only patience under a touchstone proves whether a man's temper is truly tamed.
The peacock in my garden fanned its tail and screamed at a dog, then fled as the fire in the stove spat; I thought of my own bad temper.
doha w a peacock and fire, about showing off rage

Please write a doha about how a peacock that spreads its tail in pride is beautiful until it screams, just as a person is admirable until the fire of anger leaps from him and burns away every trace of grace.
peacock, fire, temper
The peacock's tail is lovely until its voice breaks the evening, and fire in a man's temper ruins all his beauty.
Rage is a bitter gourd the angry person swallows himself, and he turns the beads of his prayer into a tangle of regret.
doha about prayer beads and a bitter gourd and rage

Write a doha showing that one who counts prayer beads all day yet keeps the bitterness of rage in his mouth is no better than a bitter gourd dipped in holy water, still bitter and unwelcome everywhere.
My aunt prays with her prayer beads at dawn, then turns bitter as a gourd when the servant is late, and I wish she would see it.
prayer beads, bitter gourd, anger
parrot, lute, calm
My parrot copied my shouting at the neighbours until the one-string lute in the corner seemed the only calm thing around.
The parrot repeats the cruel word it hears, and the one-string lute weeps; let me speak calmly where others can hear.
Compose a doha showing that a parrot repeats what it hears, so if we raise our voice in rage the whole family learns it, while the single string of a lute teaches us to stay calm.
doha w parrot and ektara about learning to stay calm

Write a doha showing that a bride carried in a palanquin sees many angry faces among the wedding guests, and that rage at a joyous occasion only spoils the day for everyone and shames the family forever.
The palanquin glides on in joy, but a man's rage at the wedding poisons the sweetness of the feast.
doha abt people fighting at a wedding with the doli passing by
At my sister's send-off, as the palanquin waited, my uncle lost his temper over a seating matter and ruined her last moments with the family.
palanquin, wedding, rage
My neighbour the yogi runs his little furnace all day yet keeps a cool face, while I lose my temper at the smallest delay.
Write a doha showing that the furnace of rage can scorch a man's soul unless he trains himself like a yogi to stay still, for the one who masters the heat inside himself is truly at peace.
The yogi tends the furnace of his mind and lets no spark of rage escape; peace is his harvest.
doha abt a furnace and a yogi, how to stay cool in rage
furnace, yogi, temper
I want a doha comparing a person's wrath to the ocean in a storm, whose waves smash everything on its shore, while patience is the still deep water beneath that harms nobody and holds everything.
doha on the ocean of anger inside me, any good lines?
When my wife and I fight, I feel like an ocean being tossed around, and I only calm down when the storm wears itself out.
ocean, stormy temper
The ocean rages on the surface but is silent in its depths; so let me sink below my fury into stillness.
doha on a lion who roars in rage and ends up alone
lion, wrath
The lion's roar shakes the valley, yet he sleeps alone; so does the angry man dine in an empty hall.
Write a doha showing that a lion who roars at every creature may be feared but lives without a friend, just as a person ruled by rage may command attention but never gains love or lasting respect.
My father roars like a lion at his family, and now my brothers rarely visit him, even though he has a lot of money.
peacock, rage
doha pls: peacock proud, but a rage it cannot hide

Compose a doha showing that the peacock's feathers are admired while its harsh scream is unwelcome, just as a person's good looks and position are forgotten when a sudden fit of rage breaks the peace.
The peacock dances in the rain with joy, yet screams at thunder; so rage strikes the beauty of a beloved soul.
My cousin looked so lovely in her wedding dress like a peacock, then she snapped at the cook and I saw the other side of her.
Last monsoon a cloud of temper settled over our family for weeks, and the only place anyone found peace was near the old village furnace.

Please write a doha showing that a cloud of furious thoughts darkens the mind just like a storm cloud darkens the day, and only the cool breeze of patience can clear it before the furnace of rage melts all.
doha about a dark cloud of anger and a furnace
The cloud of wrath gathers over the mind, and the furnace within makes thunder; let patient rain bring peace again.
cloud, furnace, rage
doha on a beggar who stays calm while a rich man rages
Write a doha showing that a beggar who bears insults without anger is richer in peace than a mighty man who is furious about the smallest loss, because rage empties the pockets of the spirit.
A beggar was kicked by a drunk man outside the school, but he just smiled and walked away, and it shamed me for all my own shouting.
The beggar holds only his bowl but also holds his calm, while the proud man loses both temper and treasure.
beggar, patience over rage
doha idea: rage is bitter, patience is jaggery

Compose a doha showing that rage is a bitter taste in the mouth that spoils every meal, while a patient and forgiving temper is like jaggery that sweetens the bitterest day and brings people close to each other.
When my mother-in-law got furious at our wedding feast, the jaggery sweets tasted like bitter herbs in everyone's mouth.
jaggery, bitter temper
Anger is the bitterness that sours even jaggery; patience is the sweetness that survives all taste.
My father's rage knocked on every door of our village until I learnt to stay quiet; now I want to keep my own door closed to such moods.

Write a doha showing that the door of the heart should be kept shut against rage as against an enemy, for once it is let in, it takes away the peace, the friends and the dignity of the entire household.
Close the door when wrath comes knocking, and it will wander off hungry into the night.
doha abt shutting the door on anger before it enters
door, shut out rage
doha for when someone insults me and I feel like exploding
Someone cut me off on the highway today, and I chased him for miles before I realised how ridiculous I looked.
anger, a bad master
Let me be master of my wrath, as a skilled rider is master of the steed, and not its prisoner.
Please compose a doha showing that anyone who cannot control his temper remains a slave, however powerful, while the person who masters his temper is a king over himself and respected by everyone.
palanquin, calm temper
Even in a palanquin of silk the angry man finds no ease, for his rage rocks the very seat he sits on.

I want a doha showing that a king travelling in a grand palanquin who loses his temper over small delays shows less greatness than a poor man who walks with peace, since rage makes the mightiest lowly.
doha on keeping calm even in a palanquin ride lol
My cousin's palanquin got stuck at the narrow lane during her wedding, and the groom's family exploded in rage for no reason.

Write a doha showing that a mountain of anger grows inside the house when family members stop speaking to each other, and that one gentle word of apology is enough to level it before it crushes everyone.
After the fight with my sister, the house felt like it sat under the weight of a mountain, heavy and silent, with neither of us willing to speak first.
house, mountain, rage
doha: rage can bring a whole house down like a mountain falling
The mountain of wrath rises in the house of the family, and none can sleep beneath its shade.
Write a doha showing that the philosopher's stone turns iron into treasure, but the touch of rage turns a precious friendship to iron, so a wise person should keep calm and protect what is precious.
The philosopher's stone makes treasure of iron, but wrath turns treasure to dust; guard your temper like a treasure.
I lost a friend of twenty years over one furious message, and it felt like losing a philosopher's stone I never knew I held.
doha with the philosopher's stone for ppl who ruin friendships in rage
philosopher's stone, rage
When my anger flared at the meeting yesterday, my own boss stopped listening, and I realised I had lost the argument the moment I raised my voice.
The calm mind is a cool morning, the angry one a restless night; choose the dawn.
keep your cool
Write a doha showing that a person who responds to insult with wrath loses twice, first his peace and then the argument, whereas the one who answers with calm wins both and keeps his friends too.
doha on not flipping out when someone provokes u
Please write a doha showing that hot temper in a young man may look like strength, but real strength is the power to hold back the blow, swallow the insult and answer with patience when provoked.
Greater than the conqueror of cities is he who conquers the storm in his own breast.
master your temper
doha pls about real strength = not losing ur temper
My teenage son punched a wall after his exam result, and I want to tell him in a doha that true strength is holding back.
well, rage, deep calm
The well stays calm however fiercely the bucket strikes, and so should the heart remain when wrath attacks.
Compose a doha showing that a deep well stays still however much water is drawn from it, just as a wise person remains calm when others throw anger at him, and shows no sign of disturbance.
doha on staying calm like a deep well when someone yells
Our village well never runs dry or muddy, and my grandmother stays just as calm when people shout at her, which I wish I could learn.
net, cotton, rage
My rage tangled me in a net of my own words, and now the cotton soft kindness I once had is hard to find.
doha with a net and cotton, anger traps u
Write a doha showing that a man in a rage is trapped in his own net of harsh words, while one who speaks soft as cotton escapes every trap of quarrel and keeps friends all his life.
Wrath casts a net around the angry man, and soft cotton words are all that could have cut him free.
The heron stands calm at the water's edge, yet inside him wrath is ready; the shroud waits for those who live for fury.
doha about a heron and a shroud, how angry ppl end up alone
heron, shroud, rage
My uncle stood like a calm heron in front of everyone, but he rained fury on his family, and now even the shroud at his funeral was arranged by strangers.
Compose a doha showing that a person who looks calm like a heron but hides rage inside is no better than a hypocrite, and the shroud will treat him and the honest alike, so he should make peace now.
I spent the whole drive back going over what my coworker said, and the longer I held on to it, the more it hurt me and not him.

Please write a doha showing that nursing a grudge keeps the wound open, and that the one who carries resentment is the one who suffers, while the other has long forgotten the incident and gone about his day.
Release your wrath like a breath, and the chest, once tight, will be wide as the open sky.
let go of rage
doha on dropping an old grudge, been stewing for years
Neither mosque nor house can shelter the man whose heart is full of wrath, for he carries the storm inside.
My brother prays at the mosque five times a day yet shouts at his family in the house all evening, and I do not understand how both coexist.
Compose a doha showing that a person who bows in the mosque but returns to his house and rages at those he loves has not understood prayer, since a calm heart is the true offering.
mosque, house, rage
doha about someone who prays at the mosque but is angry with his family
yo need a doha on how rage blinds judgment
When wrath is a dark veil upon the mind, even the clearest truth cannot be seen.
I fired a loyal worker in a fit of temper and found out the next day he had done nothing wrong.
rage blinds the mind

Compose a doha showing that anger robs a person of his sight, so that he cannot tell friend from foe, and decisions made in that darkness bring ruin that he can never repair, however much he regrets it later.
Staying at an inn full of loud, quarrelsome travellers made me see that our patience is tested like metal on a touchstone, and most of us fail.
touchstone, inn, temper
Write a doha showing that the touchstone of life tests a man's patience at every inn along the road, and he who loses his temper at small hardships fails the test, while the calm one passes.
doha about how a touchstone shows ur real temper in tough times, at an inn lol
At the inn of the world the touchstone is patience, and the angry are the ones that crack beneath it.
doha on how a tree remains calm when hit with sticks, but we shout when cursed, plus a winnowing fan
The tree gives fruit to those who strike it; teach my wrath to be winnowed by the fan of patience.
tree, winnowing fan, calm
When kids threw sticks at the tree outside my window, it kept giving shade, and I thought of how I shout at the slightest criticism, while the winnowing fan on my wall sat silent.
Compose a doha showing that a tree gives shade and fruit even to those who strike it, and that a winnowing fan separates chaff from grain, and so should we blow away rage and keep only forgiveness.
Beneath the palanquin's shade the bride sits peaceful while the groom's family rage; let calm be her dowry.
doha on rage at weddings, palanquin and shadow
The shadow of a family feud fell across my cousin's wedding, even as her palanquin was being lifted.
palanquin, shadow, rage
Write a doha showing that wrath casts a dark shadow over joyful gatherings like a wedding with the palanquin waiting, and the wise guest swallows his irritation so that the day remains happy.
The shadow of my father's temper still follows me into adulthood, making me flinch whenever someone raises their voice.
Write a doha showing that the shadow of a single man's wrath falls on his whole family, and that children grow up flinching, so a parent must learn to cool his temper before it darkens their lives.
doha on how an angry parent leaves a shadow on kids
shadow, hot temper
The shadow of wrath stretches long behind the one who rages, and falls upon the innocent.
While my wife sifts rice with the winnowing fan, I sit polishing a diamond ring and shouting about trivial matters, and she just shakes her head.
diamond, winnowing fan, rage
The winnowing fan lifts the chaff of wrath, leaving a diamond of patience shining in the palm.
Write a doha showing that the winnowing fan of calm thought blows the chaff of wrath out of the mind, leaving behind a clear diamond of patience that no one can scratch or take away.
doha with a winnowing fan and diamond, how patience beats rage
doha abt looking in a mirror when angry, so scary
In the mirror of stillness, the face of wrath is seen as ugly as it truly is.
mirror, rage, regret
When I caught my reflection in the mirror mid-shout, I barely knew the red-faced, twisted man staring back at me.
Write a doha showing that a person who looks into a mirror in the middle of a fit of rage will see a face he would never want to wear, and shame will teach him patience faster than any sermon.
